materials.content:
[1] 28th Virginia battle flag

[2] This battle flag was captured by the [First Minnesota](http://www.mnopedia.org/group/first-minnesota-volunteer-infantry-regiment) Volunteer Infantry Regiment on the third day of the Battle of Gettysburg. In the midst of Pickett's Charge on July 3, 1863, Private Marshall Sherman captured the flag from the 28th Virginia. The flag was turned into the U.S. War Department and cataloged, but by the late 19th century, it was back in Minnesota. Requests from Virginia to have the flag returned have not been succesful, and the flag is currently part of the Minnesota Historical Society collections. This object opens interesting discussions about the ownership of history.

materials.content:
[1] [Trinity Audio](https://trinityaudio.ai)player ready...

[2] Virginia shouldn’t expect any help from Minnesota Gov. Jesse Ventura in getting a blood-soaked, bullet-pierced Civil War flag returned from the Minnesota Historical Society.

[3] “Absolutely not,” the governor said Monday at the White House, where he was participating in the National Governors Association annual meeting. “Why? I mean, we won.”

[4] The Virginia Senate has approved a resolution urging Minnesota to return the flag, which was captured by the Minnesota 1st Volunteer Regiment at the Battle of Gettysburg in 1863. The Virginia House is expected to vote on the resolution soon.

[5] The Minnesota Historical Society has refused previous requests to return the flag, and its administrators say they have no intention of returning it. That could change if the Minnesota state government, which funds 65 percent of the society’s budget, gets involved, but that doesn’t seem likely.
